business.what_it_does: Newsletter software that lets writers send email newsletters, with tools for paid subscriptions, automations, sponsorships, an API, and team collaboration.
business.business_model: subscription, priced by subscriber count with paid add-ons

facts.statement: The free plan covers the first 100 subscribers at no cost, including rich text or markdown editor, sending from a custom domain, hosted newsletter archives, and privacy-first features.

provenance.quote: Absolutely nothing for your first 100 subscribers.

facts.statement: Buttondown does not take fees from paid subscribers; the customer keeps all the revenue.

facts.statement: Multiple newsletters can be created at no extra per-newsletter charge; billing is based on total subscriber count, not newsletter count.

provenance.quote: Create as many distinct newsletters as you'd like – you're only charged for your total subscribers.

provenance.quote: We're distributed around the world, and generally available from 6am-6pm US Eastern time (excluding weekends, and major holidays).

facts.statement: Buttondown is entirely browser-based with nothing to install; registration requires a browser with cookies, JavaScript and pop-ups enabled, an email address, and a password.

provenance.quote: Buttondown is entirely based in your browser. There's nothing to install, so registration is quick and easy.

facts.statement: Buttondown does not host native audio or video; it integrates with external platforms like Soundcloud, YouTube, Transistor, Spotify, and Vimeo for that content.

provenance.quote: Buttondown doesn't support native audio uploading like we do with images, nor do we have active plans on supporting it.

voice.tone: Plainspoken and a little wry, confident without hype, genuinely helpful rather than salesy
voice.rhythm: Short declarative sentences, often one or two per line; questions used as section openers; occasional long sentence followed by a clipped punch
voice.person: Writes as 'we', sometimes 'our'; product is personified ('Buttondown has you covered'); no individual human signature on marketing copy, though support replies come from named humans
exemplars: Most newsletters start as a solo effort. But as yours grows, you'll want help — an editor to catch typos, a collaborator to manage subscribers, a teammate to handle the operational side. Buttondown for Teams makes that easy.

Control exactly what each collaborator can see and do. Give your editor access to drafts but not billing. Let your marketing lead manage subscribers without touching your API keys. Everyone gets the tools they need and nothing they don't.
We know that you don't want to talk to a bot, so our small team of real humans is here to help. 💙

We're distributed around the world, and generally available from 6am-6pm US Eastern time (excluding weekends, and major holidays). Send a message and Anita, Justin, Shelley, or Steph will get back to you as soon as possible!
